questions.question: The principle of overload means that exercise training should / a). Be enjoyable at all times b). Gradually increase the training demand c). Focus only on flexibility d). Avoid fatigue
questions.solution_html:
• b) Gradually increase the training demand
  • Continuous Training
  • • Exercise is performed continuously without rest.
  • • Usually done at a steady, moderate intensity.
  • • Primarily improves aerobic endurance.
  • • Causes less fatigue compared to interval training.
  • • Example: Continuous jogging or cycling.
  • Methods of Measuring VO₂ Max
  • • Direct Method
  • • Measured in a laboratory using a treadmill or cycle ergometer.
  • • Oxygen uptake is analyzed using a metabolic gas analyzer.
questions.final_answer: Option (b) Gradually increase the training demand

questions.question: Define afterload?
questions.solution_html:

questions.question: Explain how an increase in vascular resistance affects blood pressure.
questions.solution_html:
• • Increased vascular resistance makes it harder for blood to flow through
  • vessels.

  • greater resistance.

questions.question: Explain the importance of ventricular diastole in the cardiac cycle.
questions.solution_html:
• • Ventricular diastole is the relaxation phase of the ventricles.
  • • It allows ventricular filling with blood from the atria.
  • • Adequate filling ensures an optimal stroke volume during the next
  • contraction.

questions.question: How does increased afterload influence stroke volume?
questions.solution_html:
• • Increased afterload makes it more difficult for the heart to eject blood.
  • • As a result, stroke volume decreases if cardiac contractility does not
  • increase.

questions.question: Define energy expenditure and explain its relationship with heart rate during / exercise.
questions.solution_html:
• exercise.
  • • Energy Expenditure: The amount of energy used by the body to perform
  • physical activity and maintain bodily functions.
  • • Relationship with Heart Rate
  • • Heart rate increases as exercise intensity increases.
  • • Higher intensity requires greater energy expenditure.
  • • Increased oxygen demand causes the heart to pump faster.
  • • Therefore, heart rate is often used to estimate energy expenditure.
  • • There is a near-linear relationship between heart rate and oxygen
  • consumption during moderate exercise.

questions.question: Explain how electrical impulses are generated and conducted through the heart / to produce coordinated cardiac contraction.
questions.solution_html:
• heart.
  • • Electrical impulses originate in the Sinoatrial (SA) Node, the heart's
  • natural pacemaker.
  • • The impulse spreads through both atria causing atrial contraction.
  • • It reaches the Atrioventricular (AV) Node, where a brief delay occurs.
  • • The impulse then travels through the Bundle of His.
  • • It continues through the right and left bundle branches.
  • • Finally, Purkinje fibers distribute the impulse throughout the ventricles.
  • • This coordinated conduction produces synchronized ventricular
  • contraction.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe the factors affecting ventricular filling time.
questions.solution_html:
• • Heart Rate: Increased heart rate reduces filling time.
  • • Venous Return: Greater venous return increases ventricular filling.
  • • Atrial Contraction: Enhances ventricular filling.
  • • Ventricular Compliance: More compliant ventricles fill more easily.
  • • Blood Volume: Increased blood volume improves filling.
  • • Duration of Diastole: Longer diastole allows greater filling.
questions.final_answer: • Duration of Diastole: Longer diastole allows greater filling
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Define cardiac output. Explain the formula used to calculate cardiac output and / describe its normal resting values.
questions.solution_html:
• • Cardiac output is the volume of blood pumped by the heart per minute.
  • • Formula CO = HR × SV
  • • CO = Cardiac Output
  • • HR = Heart Rate
  • • SV = Stroke Volume
  • • Normal Resting Values
  • • Average resting heart rate = 70–75 bpm.
  • • Average stroke volume = 70 mL/beat.
  • • Normal resting cardiac output ≈ 5 L/min.
  • • May increase to 20–40 L/min during intense exercise.
questions.final_answer: • May increase to 20–40 L/min during intense exercise
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Analyze how endurance training improves aerobic performance by affecting / oxygen uptake and utilization.
questions.solution_html:
• Analyze how endurance training improves aerobic performance.
  • • Increases VO₂ max.
  • • Enhances cardiac output through increased stroke volume.
  • • Improves capillary density in muscles.
  • • Increases mitochondrial number and function.
  • • Improves oxygen extraction by working muscles.
  • • Delays fatigue by enhancing aerobic energy production.
  • • Increases endurance and exercise performance.
  • • Improves efficiency of the cardiovascular and respiratory systems.
questions.final_answer: • Improves efficiency of the cardiovascular and respiratory systems
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
